author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty from the address
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty named in the address and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, case-insensitive. A blank name, or none, gives the whole directory. Paging keeps the specialty in force. No page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: Asking the directory page for a specialty by name lists only the veterinarians holding it.
Asking the machine-readable directory for a specialty by name returns only the veterinarians holding it.
A specialty name differing only by letter case matches; a fragment of a name matches nothing.
A specialty no veterinarian holds succeeds and returns the directory with no veterinarian in it.
An empty or blank specialty behaves as if none had been named, and lists every veterinarian.
A specialty name padded with leading or trailing spaces matches the same name without them.
Moving between pages of a filtered directory keeps the specialty in force, and the page counts reflect the filtered list only.
With no specialty named, both forms of the directory behave exactly as before this capability existed.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed under each, with all their specialties still shown.
non_goals: any visible control on either surface - no field, list, or button to pick a specialty (deferred to a possible follow-up request)
free-text veterinarian search, which NG-9 still declines
filtering the directory by any attribute other than specialty
naming more than one specialty in a single request
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. NG-9 narrowed by docs/adr/2026-08-24-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md; REQ-VET-003 mints the reinstated machine-readable surface and REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn. Two follow-ups sit outside this agent's write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new ADR, and the system-design.md known-defect row stating the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement is now stale (REQ-VET-003 covers it). Four open questions logged in the PRD; none blocks this slice.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice threads one optional query parameter through the vet feature package's existing shape and adds no pattern. Matching semantics belong in the repository as a Spring Data derived query, exactly as REQ-OWN-002's prefix search lives in OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith; the controller only normalizes the parameter and selects which repository method the request means, which is the delegation the architecture-principles Web controller row admits, not a business rule added to a controller. No service layer is introduced (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). Two durable-memory corrections landed with this triage: the machine-readable route's Known Defect row in system-design.md is deleted because REQ-VET-003 supplies the requirement it lacked, and docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for the non-goal ADR the PRD agent could not write.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two overloads mirroring the existing findAll pair: a paged one for /vets.html and an unpaged one for /vets. Suggested derived signatures: Page<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName, Pageable pageable) and Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName). The property path Vet.specialties -> Specialty.name (inherited from NamedEntity) resolves; IgnoreCase gives the case-insensitive whole-name equality the requirement asks for, and Distinct guards the count query against a vet joining more than one matching specialty row. VetRepository extends the bare Repository interface, which supports derived queries unchanged.

Neither new method carries @Cacheable. The specialty value is caller-supplied free text on a route needing no authentication, and the vets cache has no size limit or eviction; caching a caller-keyed lookup would let any client grow it without bound. Recorded in docs/system-design.md Threat Model.

VetController.showVetList gains @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. Normalize exactly as OwnerController.processFindForm does at line 98-104: null or blank, after strip(), means unfiltered. The existing findPaginated(page) helper takes the normalized specialty and branches between vetRepository.findAll(pageable) and the narrowed query; the PageRequest and the page-size local stay as they are, so no distinct pagination machinery is needed.

VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same parameter and the same normalization, and fills the existing Vets wrapper from the narrowed unpaged lookup. The wrapper's rendered shape is now REQ-VET-003's published contract: keep it exactly as it is. No DTO, no envelope change, no paging on this surface (paging the machine-readable directory is an explicit non-goal and an open PRD question).

vetList.html: addPaginationModel exposes the normalized specialty on the model so the seven pagination links can carry it. Replace the hand-concatenated hrefs (currently @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}) with Thymeleaf's parameter form @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value. A specialty rendered as an empty parameter is behaviorally identical to an absent one, so the unfiltered page needs no conditional.

patterns.description: the empty-search normalization and paged-lookup helper this slice mirrors: strip the parameter, treat blank as the broadest list, hand the value to a repository query method, feed the resulting Page into a private addPaginationModel
matching semantics expressed as a derived Spring Data query method rather than as controller logic; the vet filter takes the same form
the @DataJpaTest seam against the seeded H2 database where VetRepository behavior is already exercised; the query-semantics criteria belong here

risks.risk: A JOIN FETCH over the filtered association truncates each matched vet's specialty list to the one that matched, silently breaking the acceptance criterion that a vet holding several specialties is still shown with all of them.
risks.mitigation: Use a plain derived query with no fetch join. Vet.specialties is already @ManyToMany(fetch = EAGER), so Hibernate loads the full collection by a secondary select and every specialty survives. Cover it with a test on a vet holding two specialties, filtered by one.

risks.risk: The four semantic criteria (case-insensitive match, no prefix match, surrounding-space trim, filtered page counts) cannot be observed in VetControllerTests, which stands VetRepository up as a @MockitoBean and therefore returns whatever the test tells it to.
risks.mitigation: Split the coverage by where the behavior lives. VetControllerTests verifies parameter plumbing: that a blank value reaches the unfiltered path, that a value reaches the narrowed path stripped, that the model and the JSON document carry the narrowed list. The matching and paging semantics get a repository test against the real seeded H2, alongside the existing shouldFindVets in ClinicServiceTests. Mocking the repository is also the weaker position under testing-principles.md, which admits mocks only at system boundaries.

risks.risk: Pagination over a join to a to-many association can push Hibernate into applying firstResult/maxResults in memory, which would leave the filtered page counts subtly wrong.
risks.mitigation: findAll(Pageable) already pages the same eagerly-fetched entity today, so the shape is proven; confirm it for the narrowed query with a repository-level paging assertion on the real database rather than trusting the mocked controller test.

risks.risk: Concatenating the raw specialty into pagination hrefs would emit an unencoded caller-supplied value into the page.
risks.mitigation: Use Thymeleaf's @{path(param=value)} form, which encodes; never build the query string by string concatenation. Thymeleaf's default expression escaping covers the rendered text, and the value reaches the database only through a parameterized JPA query.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. Durable-memory writes accompanying this triage: docs/adr/README.md index row for 2026-08-24-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md; docs/system-design.md drops the now-stale machine-readable-route Known Defect row, wires Implements for Vets (REQ-VET-003), VetRepository (REQ-VET-004) and VetController (REQ-VET-003, REQ-VET-004), records that the Vets shape is a published contract, names the specialty parameter under Security Context inputs, adds the unbounded-cache-key Threat Model row, and narrows Open Question 5 to the unfiltered methods. No ADR: the design adds no hard-to-reverse choice beyond what 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization and the non-goal ADR already record. Observation outside this slice, offered so it is not made worse: both paged controllers pass page - 1 to PageRequest.of unguarded, so ?page=0 raises and reaches the error page. Pre-existing on /owners and /vets.html alike, breaches no requirement, and is not this slice's to fix. Four PRD open questions touch this area (naming the shown specialty on the page, more than one specialty at once, paging the machine-readable directory, distinguishing an unknown specialty from an unheld one); the contract implements the narrowest reading of each and none blocks implementation.

author: feature-implementer
summary: Optional specialty filter on both vet directory surfaces. VetRepository gains two uncached derived queries (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, unpaged and paged); VetController normalizes the parameter (null/blank/whitespace after strip means the whole directory) and selects the narrowed or unfiltered lookup on /vets.html and /vets; vetList.html pagination hrefs move to Thymeleaf's URL-encoding @{path(param=value)} form and carry the specialty. Six repository tests against the seeded H2 cover whole-name and case-insensitive matching, no prefix match, an unheld specialty, all specialties preserved on a multi-specialty vet, and filtered page counts; nine controller tests cover parameter plumbing, blank-as-absent, padded values, empty results at 200, unparameterized behavior unchanged, and pagination links carrying the parameter. Gradle format tasks in this project are format/checkFormat, not the formatJava/checkJavaFormat names in CLAUDE.md.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: VetController.showVetList/showResourcesVetList mirror OwnerController.processFindForm's null-to-blank normalization and dual-path (filtered/unfiltered) lookup shape exactly, keeping the slice consistent with the codebase's existing pattern

normalizeSpecialty and findVets are small, single-purpose, descriptively named private helpers with no side effects; javadoc on both new VetRepository derived-query methods explains the whole-name/case-insensitive match and states the deliberate absence of @Cacheable with its rationale inline, which is exactly the kind of non-obvious design choice a future reader needs surfaced at the point of reading rather than only in a design doc

the addPaginationModel comment ('the pagination links carry the filter, so an unfiltered page renders it empty') makes the sanctioned empty-vs-absent-parameter tradeoff legible in the code itself, not just in the design record

vetList.html's seven pagination hrefs uniformly adopt Thymeleaf's @{path(param=value)} encoding form, replacing the prior hand-concatenated string, with no leftover string-concatenation instance found on a sweep of the template
no service layer added (consistent with the recorded ADR), no JOIN FETCH, no DTO/envelope change to Vets — all as specified and correctly not re-litigated
checkFormat and compileJava/compileTestJava both pass clean

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Reflected-input XSS: all five th:href attributes in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html (lines 30, 35, 40, 46, 52) use Thymeleaf's link-expression parameter form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}. No hand-concatenated query string survives, so the caller-supplied value is URL-encoded as a query parameter and HTML-escaped as an attribute value. The path segment is a static literal and is not caller-influenced.

Escaping sweep across the class: grep for th:utext and inlined [( )] unescaped output across src/main/resources/templates/ returns nothing, so no template disables Thymeleaf's default escaping. The only other occurrence of the name specialty in the template (line 20) is a th:each loop variable over vet.specialties rendered with th:text, scoped to the table body and distinct from the model attribute used by the pagination block outside it; it does not shadow or reflect the request value.

Model exposure: VetController.addPaginationModel (line 60) publishes only the normalized specialty, and the /vets JSON surface (showResourcesVetList) serializes the Vets wrapper alone and does not echo the parameter back. No other sink consumes the value.

Unbounded cache keys: @Cacheable is genuinely absent from both new overloads in VetRepository.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase (unpaged line 72, paged lines 84-85). The diff's only @Cacheable occurrence is the pre-existing pair on findAll; the two other matches are Javadoc prose recording the deliberate omission. An unauthenticated caller therefore creates no cache entry from a chosen specialty value. The docs/system-design.md Threat Model row states the residual page-number-keyed growth honestly as Partial rather than overclaiming; that growth is pre-existing and outside this slice.

Injection: no @Query, createQuery, createNativeQuery, EntityManager use, or string concatenation into a query appears anywhere in the diff. Both new methods are Spring Data derived queries, so the specialty reaches the database only as a bound parameter. This matches the existing SQL-injection mitigation recorded in the system-design Threat Model.

Input normalization: normalizeSpecialty (VetController line 85) maps null to the empty string and strips the value, and both branch points test isEmpty(), so no null or blank value reaches a repository call and no NPE path exists on the unauthenticated route.

Denial of service: a pathological or oversized specialty value is bound as a query parameter on a route that creates no cache entry and allocates nothing proportional to the input beyond the string itself; the worst case is one indexed join lookup returning no rows. No new amplification primitive is introduced.

Secrets: a case-insensitive sweep of added lines for password, secret, token, key, and credential patterns matches only descriptive prose in docs/system-design.md. No credential, key, or endpoint literal is added.

Supply chain: the change set touches no build file - build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are unmodified - so the dependency graph and its CVE exposure are unchanged by this slice. No new third-party import appears in the diff.

findings.description: The Veterinarian directory narrative names the literal query-parameter identifier: "The specialty is named in the address, as `specialty`". This is the one place in the PRD that names a concrete interface identifier (a URL query-string key) rather than describing behavior; no sibling requirement (REQ-OWN-002's search, REQ-LANG-001's locale switch) names its parameter this way, and the PRD Boundary Rule's litmus test (would it change under a different interface technology — a header, a path segment, a form field) puts the exact key name in system-design.md, not prd.md. system-design.md's Security Context row already carries the abstract version correctly ("Query parameters naming a page and a specialty on both veterinarian directory routes") without the literal string. Reword the PRD sentence to state the behavior without the backticked key, e.g. "The specialty is named in the address, and nothing on the page offers it", and let system-design.md carry the literal parameter name if needed.

approved_aspects: NG-9 narrowing follows the b67f301/NG-4/NG-5 convention exactly: non-goal ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-24-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md with Non-goal: NG-9 in Implementation, docs/adr/README.md index row added, NG-9 table row rewritten with the exception clause plus a "Narrowed 2026-08-24 — [ADR]" pointer, and the Non-Goals preamble updated from two to three decided rows with the veterinarian clause correctly scoped separately from the still-undecided pet/visit clauses.

REQ-VET-002 withdrawal record is internally consistent with REQ-VET-003: the Superseded entry and the revisited open question both name REQ-VET-003 as the reinstated surface, state the withdrawn ID is never reused, and no document still calls the /vets JSON route an orphaned artifact — the stale system-design.md Known Defect row was correctly deleted.

REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 are testable, carry Done-when bullets covering every acceptance criterion, and stay behavioral — no signatures, no code identifiers, no mechanism beyond the one flagged finding.

Every cross-reference checked resolves: ADR links to prd.md#non-goals and prd.md#req-vet-003, PRD links to system-design.md#contracts/#security-context/#known-defects, and the adr/README.md index and template conventions all match existing anchors and headings.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All 15 new test methods in this slice use `should{Verb}...` or `show{Endpoint}...` names instead of the project's BDD naming school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`, testing-principles.md § Test Naming), which explicitly applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. The pre-existing `shouldFindVets` in ClinicServiceTests is grandfathered; these are new. Affected: shouldFindOnlyVetsHoldingTheGivenSpecialty, shouldMatchTheSpecialtyNameRegardlessOfCase, shouldNotMatchAPartialSpecialtyName, shouldFindNoVetsForASpecialtyNoVetHolds, shouldKeepEverySpecialtyOfAVetMatchedByOneOfThem, shouldCountPagesOverTheFilteredVetsOnly (ClinicServiceTests); showVetListHtmlForSpecialty, showVetListHtmlForSpecialtyPaddedWithSpaces, showVetListHtmlForNoSpecialtyHolder, showVetListHtmlForBlankSpecialty, showVetListHtmlCarriesTheSpecialtyInPaginationLinks, showResourcesVetListForSpecialty, showResourcesVetListForSpecialtyPaddedWithSpaces, showResourcesVetListForNoSpecialtyHolder, showResourcesVetListForBlankSpecialty (VetControllerTests). The names also name the method under test (showVetListHtml, showResourcesVetList) rather than the outcome, which the school's rename-survival test rejects.
findings.fix: Rename to the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` form. The controller-side names largely match the prd-entry's own test_names field (line 2 of the ledger): theVetListShouldShowOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty, theVetListShouldTrimSurroundingSpacesFromTheSpecialtyName, theVetListShouldShowNoVetsWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty, theVetListShouldShowEveryVetWhenTheSpecialtyIsBlank, theVetListPaginationShouldKeepTheSpecialtyAcrossPages, theVetResourceShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty, theVetResourceShouldTrimSurroundingSpacesFromTheSpecialtyName, theVetResourceShouldShowNoVetsWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty, theVetResourceShouldReturnEveryVetWhenNoSpecialtyIsGiven. For the repository tests, e.g. theSpecialtyQueryShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingIt, theSpecialtyQueryShouldMatchRegardlessOfCase, theSpecialtyQueryShouldNotMatchAPartialName, theSpecialtyQueryShouldReturnNoVetsForAnUnheldSpecialty, theSpecialtyQueryShouldKeepAllSpecialtiesOfAMatchedVet, theSpecialtyQueryShouldCountPagesOverFilteredVetsOnly.

approved_aspects: Every stated acceptance criterion is pinned down by a test: whole-name match, case-insensitive match, no-prefix match, unheld-specialty empty result at 200, blank/whitespace treated as absent, leading/trailing-space trim, multi-specialty vet keeps all specialties when matched by one, filtered page counts, pagination links carrying the parameter, and unparameterized behavior unchanged on both surfaces

The mocked-repository/real-repository split follows the design ruling correctly: VetControllerTests only asserts plumbing (stubbed input reaches the model/JSON unchanged, stripped value reaches the mocked repository call), while every semantic matching and paging claim is proven against the real seeded H2 database in ClinicServiceTests — no test asserts a semantic claim through the mock
No new mocks introduced; the pre-existing @MockitoBean on VetRepository is reused exactly as testing-principles.md's grandfather clause for existing mock-framework usage permits

AssertJ used fluently throughout ClinicServiceTests (extracting/containsExactlyInAnyOrder/isEmpty); four-phase structure with blank-line separation and no phase comments in all new tests; all 15 new tests and the full suite pass (./gradlew test)

The repository test proving Vet.specialties is not truncated when matched by one of several (shouldKeepEverySpecialtyOfAVetMatchedByOneOfThem) directly covers the design-block's flagged JOIN FETCH risk

Round 5 narrowed reach further than round 4: the only file changed since the round-3 approved tree is VetControllerTests.java, verified independently by two reviewers via blob hashes rather than by report. The template rewrite still executes on every vet page render, and that is the one live surface; it is now pinned in both branches by a matched pair of tests.

semantic_surprise.note: Re-read the full production delta rather than the round narratives, since production is byte-identical to round 3 and could have drifted under five template mutation cycles. It has not. addPaginationModel exposes null when the normalized filter is empty and the template derives the filtered flag once from a null check on the specialty, so each of the five anchors picks between a link expression naming page and specialty and one naming page alone; an unfiltered page renders /vets.html?page=2 exactly as the pre-slice preprocessed literal did. The null-in-the-view versus empty-string-in-the-controller split is a trap in principle, but the two values are computed at different call sites, the divergence is commented where it happens, and a missing attribute falls to the unfiltered branch rather than failing. normalizeSpecialty, the derived whole-name IgnoreCase finders and the deliberate cache omission are unchanged and still match their Javadoc. No hidden behavior.

test_adequacy.note: The gap I raised at line 49 is closed, and I re-derived the closure from the source rather than from the round-5 reports. theVetListPaginationShouldKeepTheSpecialtyAcrossPages now stubs a page of one vet at PageRequest.of(2,5) over 25 elements, so currentPage is 3 and totalPages is 5: both pagination conditions hold, all five link kinds render as real anchors, and the four icons target four distinct pages (1, 2, 4, 5), so no assertion can be satisfied by a neighbour. Each paginationIcon matcher requires the href and the icon class inside one tag, with a negated-character-class gap that cannot cross a tag boundary, and the numbered-loop anchor is pinned by literal containsString with its page text, which no icon anchor carries. Counting both tests, all ten template branches (five link sites, filtered and unfiltered) are now individually pinned, plus the unfiltered test's page-wide assertion that no specialty parameter appears anywhere. Below the controller, ClinicServiceTests exercises the derived finders against a real database, including a page of size one over two surgeons asserting totalElements 2 and totalPages 2, which is the assertion that would catch a distinct-join count bug.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round 5 ran the full battery over the full diff (high risk: multi-module, oversize, design-revision) and all four approved. Three filed empty findings lists, each on independently produced evidence rather than on the implementer's word: security re-derived the production blob hashes against the round-3 approved tree, test-reviewer mutated the last-page anchor itself and watched the test fail, then restored and re-ran clean, and code-quality re-ran the class twice after a clean recompile. The one finding on the board is code-quality's helper-placement note: tag autofix, severity fixable, no bar_clause and no escalate, and its own text calls it a scan-order nit rather than a defect. The schema reserves bar_clause for findings that target a quality-bar clause and directs it to be omitted for procedural items, so the harness's designed hedge signal is absent here. The standing fragment-refactor advisory is likewise non-blocking across four rounds, and its author now argues the duplication is safer than before because every copy is pinned by a failing assertion. Both are maintainability items left open by choice, not reservations about the change.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries and zero consultations across all five rounds. The single design revision remains the NG-9 narrowing ADR, which is the slice recording a product decision inside its triage rather than fighting it, and the PRD, system-design and ADR index edits all trace to that decision or to REQ-VET-003's reinstatement. Round 5 was test-file-only, confirmed by two reviewers against the round-4 tree, and added no production API, no visible page control and no new file. The tree the reviewers approved is the tree I graded, so nothing drifted after approval.

rationale: The filtered-side mirror gap I flagged is genuinely closed, not merely re-reviewed: page 3 of 5 renders all five anchors at four distinct targets, and each is pinned by href and class together. All ten template branches are now covered. Two non-blocking style advisories stay open by choice. Confirm and merge.
